title: Southampton and the EFL warning: the mockery line is being drawn now
body:
The EFL has warned clubs against mocking Southampton, and the Spygate reference sits at the centre of the message [S1].

Sky Sports carried the story under a headline that ties the club and the Spygate reference together, and that pairing is the heart of the matter [S1]. The warning targets clubs that mock Southampton and use the Spygate reference as a punchline, according to the report [S1]. The league is making a point about where a rivalry jibe stops and something harder begins [S1].

But there is a difference between a chant and a campaign. When one club becomes the punchline for a wider grievance, the line blurs, and the side on the receiving end tends to remember who joined in.

With no form or prediction to weigh, this story is about principle rather than points. The fairest reading is that the league wants the jokes kept within limits. The real test is whether that message is applied evenly from one fixture to the next, and the manager who gets caught out by a warning like this will want to see that consistency too.

The Touchline Take: one to keep an eye on, because a warning is only as good as its enforcement.
